Team —

- A small staging pool (warm nodes) we can spin up in 2–3 days to buffer initial traffic.
- Clear gating signals to trigger bulk provisioning from OEM/cloud (purchase/commit).
- The minimum list of artifacts we need to share with vendors to get accurate ETA (model footprint, expected steady RPS, 95p latency target, and preferred quantization).

Attached is a rough diagram of the staging-pool idea — small warm cache + autoscaler policy that opens reserved lanes by deal maturity. Need a short checklist and timeline that I can share with legal/procurement.

1) Marissa — draft the procurement gating checklist and vendor lead times (what do we need to see from Nebula before we hit the 30% commit).
2) Ben — map the deal milestones to capacity buckets (staging -> soft-commit -> committed).
3) Karthik — confirm whether the autoscale policy proposed in the diagram can be enforced across Dedicated and Private deployments (are there any infra blockers?).

Target: have a one-pager to share with Atlas and Dell procurement by EOD Monday so we can start parallel quoting.

Thanks —

Vanessa — thanks, this is helpful. Quick draft below (lean checklist + timelines). I attached a spreadsheet with vendor lead time assumptions (oem_quote_v2.xlsx).

Procurement gating checklist (suggested):
- Signed MOU or LOI from customer stating estimated month-1 QPS and committed seats (if available).
- Technical footprint: peak concurrent tokens, model name/version, preferred quantization (int8/4bit) and average sequence length.
- Security/compliance addendum (SOC2 / data handling) if Private/VPC required.
- Forecast: 3-month ramp schedule with confidence level (low/med/high).
- PO trigger thresholds: staging threshold (e.g., 10% of expected sustained RPS) to start warm pool, soft-commit (30%) to initiate OEM quote lock, committed (70–100%) for capacity purchase.

Vendor lead-time assumptions (high level):
- OEM (hardware orders): 8–14 weeks typical, 4–6 weeks expedited if stock and regional shipping OK (requires down payment).
- Hyperscalers (reserved instances/pools): 2–6 weeks depending on quota approval and onboarding docs.
- Local supply contingencies (refurb/short-term rental): 1–3 weeks but higher unit cost and limited sku.

Gating signal recommendations:
1) Technical readiness sign-off from applied ML (model and perf profile).
2) LOI indicating month-1 target and ramp curve.
3) Procurement ready doc set (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams) to begin quota requests.

Timeline ask: if Nebula can provide the LOI by 9/6 we can submit quota and OEM RFQs the week of 9/7; earliest delivery mid-Oct in optimistic path.

I also put a note in the sheet with a conservative buffer (add 3 weeks) for shipping and customs in case of cross-border OEM.

Marissa
Sr. Program Manager, Capacity Planning

Adding a couple tactical items from GTM/deal side: 

- Deal milestones mapping to capacity buckets:
  * Sig/LOI (T-0): authorize 1–2 warm nodes (~10% of target) in staging pool. Allows smoke tests and demos.
  * PO/Initial commit (T+2 weeks): upsell to soft-commit (30% capacity). Begin reservation discussions with OEM + submit hyperscaler quotas.
  * Production sign-off (T+6–8 weeks): finalize committed capacity and start procurement orders for remaining 70%.

- Financial lever: propose a 12-week credit holdback on hardware invoices tied to performance SLAs — helps get OEM to accept smaller initial down payments. I’ll run this with finance.

- Risk buffer: recommend keeping a 15% short-term rental buffer (partner rental pool) for the first 6 weeks post-onramp to absorb any OEM shipping slips. Estimated cost impact is in Marissa's spreadsheet.

FYI I pinged Sam at Nebula asking for the LOI and the month-1 QPS estimate; Sam said they can get a preliminary LOI and perf targets by EOD today (they're finalizing procurement approvals).

Ben
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
